title: The Next Step
body:
Craft is a fantastic tool. I’m an avid user of Notion and other popular organization and productivity apps, and I genuinely think Craft has everything it needs to become the next big thing. I especially love the tagging system — it’s one of the best I’ve used.
There is one small feature I’d love to see, though, and while it may sound minor, it would make a big difference to my personal workflow: the ability to freely place blocks next to each other on a page without having to put them inside a separate card, page, or special container.
For example, if I have three embedded videos, I’d love to simply drag them side by side and create a horizontal layout. Notion makes this very easy — you can just grab a block and pull it next to another one. In Craft, achieving something similar currently requires adding another layer of structure.
It’s a tiny detail compared with everything Craft already does so well, but for the way I work, it’s probably the one thing Notion still has over Craft for me personally.

title: A lot of good stuff, some baggage
body:
Craft looks great--much better than other notes apps I've tried.  

I love all the options for formatting (color, font, etc).  I use a ton of visual formatting in my notes to make them eye-catching, and this remains a struggle for most, if not all notes apps.

That said, the application of those formatting options is often clunky, unpredictable, or frustrating, much of which is derived from the whole "blocks" business, which feels like a weird and unnecessary thing when the app could simply treat text as any word processor does and let you edit elements discreetly instead of changes automatically being applied across whole areas of information just because they aren't separated by a paragraph break.

Why is getting consistent paragraph breaks difficult, sometimes it double spaces, sometimes single and I can't edit that easily because efforts to delete the extra space instead only seem to delete the text formatting of the information after the cursor?  The accumulation of these weird little behaviors adds up to a sense of overall frustration when it is not intuitively clear how to achieve the results I'm after.

Most frustrating thing though, by far, is that unless I'm missing it, there is no undo button on the actual editing screen, so every time I make any mistake or the app doesn't behave as expected, I have to hit done, then another button to access the nested "undo" option and then two more buttons just to get back to where I was editing the note.  Now imagine doing that 30 times in an hour.  

Just put undo/redo on the primary note editing screen and save us so much needless back-and-forth and this would be worth a full extra star immediately.

title: Feedback for Craft Team: Persistent "Zombie" Entry in Spotlight Settings
body:
Subject: Technical Issue: Persistent "com.lukilabs.lukiapp" entry in macOS System Settings after uninstallation

I am writing to report a persistent technical issue regarding the uninstallation footprint of Craft on macOS (Mac Store version).

[Issue Description] After uninstalling Craft, a "zombie" entry for com.lukilabs.lukiapp remains visible in System Settings > Siri & Spotlight > Search Results (App Results). Even after the app is physically deleted, the entry persists in the UI (sometimes with a generic icon).

[Technical Investigation & Attempts] As a technical user, I have attempted the following high-level troubleshooting steps to no avail:

LaunchServices Reset: Ran lsregister -u on the specific path and attempted to kill the database. lsregister -dump previously showed the app indexed in .Trash, but even after clearing the Trash and unregistering, the UI remains.

Preference Cleaning: Manually cleaned com.apple.Spotlight.plist by removing com.lukilabs.lukiapp from EnabledPreferenceRules and clearing queryViewOptions.

Spotlight Reindexing: Executed mdutil -E / and deleted ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight.

Cache Clearing: Purged com.apple.SystemSettings and cfprefsd caches.

[Observation] It appears that because Craft is a Mac Catalyst app, it may be leaving behind stale metadata in the CoreSpotlight private store or the macOS SyncedPreferences (iCloud KVS) that isn't being properly flushed upon deletion. This results in a "ghost" toggle in the system settings that cannot be removed by standard user-level maintenance.

[Request] Could you please investigate if the app can explicitly call index.deleteAllSearchableItems or a similar cleanup routine during its lifecycle, or provide a standalone "Deep Clean" script/command for users who encounter this "zombie" entry?

Thank you for your attention to this detail. Craft is a great app, and I'd love to see a cleaner "exit" for the Mac version.

I’m working on financials and taxes and desperately needed system to work. ChatGPT helped me figure out that maybe it was a space constraint and that using multiple spaces could make room for data. After being down for about a half a week:  the solution,  you guessed it,  pay more money for a different version with more space… Did I have an alternative? Nope.  Like I said: great app in many ways but if you don’t like being held hostage, be aware. You’ll never be able to change apps without starting from scratch      …. and God-forbid you actually need technical support. This one’s kind of like learning the brother you love, is stealing from you. Too bad because up to this point this was one of the few services that I felt I could count on  in my life & really our overall economy that is quickly evolving to quantity over quality … which translates to where companies focus more on marketing than Support because this way they just replace the users they lose. So yes, this is great for I'm going to assume 50% of the users who only use blank white documents in the app, but given the customization features that the app touts, I'm willing to bet most of its users do use templates. And yet when Siri 2.0 comes out or some other better automation service, this app won't be ready for that because people will be restricted to using the app through AI with only blank documents.

This app is awesome for staying organized and planning. It’s been so helpful for me with my business. There’s a lot I like about it and very little I don’t like. I don’t really use the AI features, but I wish it could design and structure documents for you. 

Improvements I’d like to see:
- It would be easier to find documents when you first open the app if you could see them in list view divided by Spaces and folders. Visuals are important when trying to find things, so use cells and colors to separate categories. Or let us customize our own. 
- Filters that permanently stay on for the recent docs page- the one that is displayed when first opening the app- would be amazing. They would need to to stay on even after closing the app. 
- The tables need a little work and more customization. Viewing them on a phone is cumbersome. 
- I would love to have an option to set documents into a view only mode not just for invitees but also myself. That way I can use the checklists and not accidentally start editing the texts or anything else. 
- overall more flexibility with moving cells and texting editing would be cool, though it’s already really good! 
- I’ve noticed that when I invite someone via email and text them a link they end up requesting access anyways. And they end up showing as two separate users even when it’s the same email address. 

The app is well worth the subscription and I love the features. I can’t wait to see what the devs come up with down the road!

title: Awesome! But could use some new AI models.
body:
Craft is an excellent notes, productivity, and AI writing app. However, like most apps, it has room for improvement, particularly regarding its AI models.

The local AI features are impressive, but it would be beneficial to include more modern models, such as Qwen 3 with 0.6B parameters for local processing, or Llama 3.3. For cloud-based AI, while Craft already offers GPT-4o, this model feels somewhat dated now. Adding Claude 3.5 Haiku or Claude Opus 4 would be valuable upgrades. Alternatively, if sticking with OpenAI, o4-mini would provide a fast, intelligent, and cost-effective option.

Beyond AI capabilities, Craft's interface is stylish and well-deserving of its App Store Design Award. If you want an alternative to Apple's built-in Notes app, or if you don't have a newer iPhone with Apple Intelligence but still want AI-powered note-taking, Craft is an excellent choice.

title: Not accessible…

Sadly, I was very disappointed to discover that, as a visually impaired VoiceOver screen reader user, the app is not well thought out for users such as myself.  All the controls are read aloud as text boxes, and the main documents are completely inaccessible on Mac.  I give the app 2 stars for concept, and it likely works great for sighted individuals, but I would say that there was little to no consideration of visually impaired or blind users when creating this app.  If you rely on accessibility features such as VoiceOver, you’ll need to look elsewhere at this point.

title: Good developers build good apps. Great developers try, and listen to feedback when they get it wrong
body:
My favorite thing about Craft isn’t just that it was a good personal database app when I started using it. (even then, it felt like the more native, refined app I always wanted every time I tried Notion and found myself hating the very “web first” feel of it. 

It’s that the developers have made wrong turns as they continue to improve it, and they’ve listened when users like me hated the changes. They found ways to keep giving me the experience that brought us here in the first place. 

I do hope to see less focus on AI moving forward. It’s a frustrating experience that I want no part in. I just want speed, responsiveness, and a great document creating and linking experience. The Mac app feels like it’s suffering more from bloat right now, and editing text is getting worse. But here on iPhone, I’m still loving it, and it pulls me more and more away from typical note taking apps and into Craft where I can link and organize everything to the level I like to. 

Finding a balance between making it immediate to create a new document, and making it possible to navigate the depths of a ton of organized information, is one of the hardest things I can think of for a notes app, but Craft does this really well. It’s important, and it’s been improving since I started using it. I hope Craft keeps focusing its effort on these kinds of refinements.

title: Long Live The Craft!
body:
This app has been a true game-changer relative to note taking for my graduate courses.  Recently, I've taking to outlining chapters from my reading into succinct, bite-size notes. This is perfect for active recall sessions via the toggle button.  Likewise, I'm also using it as a repository for information I'll need to keep long-term.  It's been brilliant...not to mention how inviting the notes look with a little TLC applied. It makes going back into my notes less of a chore! 

That said, today Craft introduced Tables!  That is another great and much need addition.  Give Craft credit for hearing its consumers and making attempts to apply those suggestions offered.  At a quick look, and limited use, Tables is welcomed in my note taking.  I'll likely create a Table Template that I can use for specific notes that require graphed information. 

Finally, a word of suggestion.  With Tables comes great responsibility.  One area that will need to be incorporated, in my opinion, is the ability to Table & Database.  Perhaps the only reason I continue to use Notion, is for the sheer strength of maninpulating data in its database function.  If Craft offered that, I'd likely not need to use Notion at all, since I like the native capability and privacy of Craft.  Collections is a great step in the direction -- not quite as functional as Notion. 

Great app!  I'm super-impressed!  I look forward to future updates and continuing to enjoy working in the Craft app.  It's made my digital note-taking life so much more navigable! 

Kudos!!!!!

PS. UPDATE MONTHS LATER : Craft continues to be impressive.  Again, it's been a game-changer for my graduate courses.  If you haven't looked at Craft, give it a shot.  Put in a little time to learn how to make notes, how to add asthetics, and how to best organize & navigate your notes.  Once you've done that, it should prove a must have, Top Tier, note-taking app. I use it daily. 

PSS.  UPDATE EVEN MORE MONTHS LATER : The addition of Tasks is a nice touch as well!  Very helpful and useful.  Have fully revamped my Craft spaces and layout to streamline my notes process and to incorporate Tasks accordingly. I especially like the ability to pin docs with Tasks and move Tasks to and from as necessary. Tasks for the win!

title: One-Stop Shop for Organizing Your Life!!
body: I wanted to leave a review for this app 1) to ensure the Craft team’s hard work and creativity gets recognized and 2) so others who love visually appealing and functional apps find this amazing tool! I have used multiple apps in the past to try and quilt together the features found in a calendar app, reminders/tasks app, journaling app etc. so I could “finally” get a holistic picture of what I have going on in my life. Not because I enjoyed using several apps - trust me I didn’t - but because there just wasn’t one that I could find to do everything I needed it to do. I honestly can’t remember how I eventually found Craft, but I remember being suspicious at first that it could actually meet my needs. I downloaded it, then uninstalled it, then re-downloaded it again etc. :) but am happy I came back to the app and really dug into the functionality and features, because once I got used to it, the potential use cases started popping up all over and now I can confidently say that I use Craft for everything - my personal journal (I love the freedom to type an entry or insert a handwritten entry using the Sketch block feature) my planner for work (I use the daily notes feature to connect my work notes to a calendar date so I can take meeting notes and record ideas etc.), logs for hobbies, my meal planning log and recipe inventory, shopping lists, organizing my solopreneur business ideas, and for creative writing. Being able to setup a visual backdrop and create beautiful themes for projects really helps get me in the right mindset for writing and creating like no other tool has. It’s part of my morning ritual now and I truly enjoy working within Craft. As a corporate employee, I can tell you there’s value in taking the time to visually setup a creative space to help shift your mindset at the end of a work day (or before you even get started) towards creative work. Love, love, love, this app!!! :)

title: Craft Keeps Getting Better
body:
I’ve absorbed everything from the recent v3 update and I can’t believe how far this app has come. I switched to Craft back when it was just another one of the aesthetic writing apps, but it had the extra features of blocks, cards and subpages that I needed.  Now there are so many capabilities in this app that it’s up there with the Affinity apps, but for creating productivity.

They keep adding more sophisticated features without losing the UI aesthetic. Everything looks good and I want to use this app for everything.

Task management in Craft is about to replace one of my other apps. I used to keep a big list of tasks in my daily note and I had to keep moving the unfinished ones up to the current day. Now I can keep tasks in their context where they belong and just go over to the tasks tab to see them all and schedule them.  My daily note has separate UI to show just today’s tasks, which is way less overwhelming than a long list of tasks to pick from for today.

I wasn’t sure about the collection feature when it was first hyped, but it just clicked for me, and it’s now the feature I’m excited to see more development on.

Remember when Craft users were like “We need tags”, and Craft was like “We got something coming”, and we were like “What’s taking so long? it’s just a search construct with some UI”.  Now Craft has given us tags.. along with any other custom fields we want.. that we can apply to sub-pages within the context of a collection that exists as a table in some document that can be searched and organized and even related to other collections.  It’s got some limitations and flaws but it’s very usable and I’ve already found several uses and I can’t wait for more updates.

I’m a software engineer and Craft gives me that tingly feeling when so much information is so well organized. Craft is one subscription I am not cancelling!

title: Best writing app I’ve ever had
body:
I remember a few years ago feeling like I could never find a very well-designed writing app. It always felt like some aspects of the various apps were good, but they all had pain points that used to annoy me a lot. 

Then I found Craft and it felt like a perfect fit. I still try other writing apps from time to time out of curiosity, but none of them feel like this one does.

The unique feature I like best is the way I can easily write or take notes in the app (or even in the web-app), and then easily share a link with others as a beautifully presented website. It’s really clean, professional, and stylish, very unlike a typical “doc” that normally gets shared. This is a writing app that can connect me with other people in a way that makes me both look and feel good to them and myself as well.

My 9-year old son uses it too! His favorite features are the amazing styling options, which he can tweak to his hearts content to make his writing look good. He says every time they add a new feature, he wonders, “Why didn’t I think of that before?” 

Definitely give it a try and see if it works for you as well as it does for me! If you have tried it before, come back and have another look. They have recently added a lot of new features like task management and data collections, and I’m personally quite impressed.

Naturally, the first thing I try to do is create some notes and then collect them on a document, styled as Craft’s cards or pages. Guess what? You can’t. Unless you had the foresight to create a note as a card, you’re stuck with plain text links. Guess what happens when I try to style those plain links as cards? Instead of doing that, craft creates a new, empty page with my link as the title. The best part is that you can’t even use the link anymore because tapping it only opens the keyboard. 

It feels as though everything is like this. When I actually try to DO something that leans into Craft’s strengths. It just pushes back. I really wanted it to be my end all app, but it sure won’t at this rate.

title: Beautiful but getting bloated
body:
Beautiful app with great mobile interactions - I can do most things comfortably with my thumb. The AI features work well and feel worth the subscription price.

But the navigation is just confusing. The home screen feels like a confusing mash-up of a Feed and Search that never clicked for me. The Organize screen would make more sense as home, but it's so visually busy that I often lose track of what I'm doing. I really dislike the document previews in the sidebar and wish I could edit them or turn them off altogether—I don’t need to know what the document looks like just let me read what it’s called.

With Craft 3 adding Collections (a good addition but still no Tags) on top of a new focus on Tasks and Calendar, it feels like the app has lost sight of its core purpose as a document editor and is instead taking a new kitchen sink approach. Taken together, the new features have made the app more complicated than I bargained for.

title: A beautiful and practical platform
body:

My favorite use case is the daily calendar. I created a template to record my top three goals for the day, along with space to capture what I accomplish at work and at home. It’s easy to insert the template using the slash (/) command.
